title: Cognitive restructuring
content: Notice an unhelpful automatic thought, gently examine the evidence for and against it, and construct a more balanced, realistic alternative. Works best one thought at a time, with curious questions rather than lecturing.
license: Public Domain (U.S. NIMH) — technique described in NIMH CBT material

title: Behavioral activation
content: When low mood shrinks activity, schedule small, meaningful or pleasant actions to rebuild momentum. Action often comes before motivation, so start tiny and specific.
license: Public Domain (U.S. NIMH) — technique described in NIMH depression material

title: Cognitive defusion
content: Create distance from a sticky thought by noticing it as a thought — for example, 'I'm having the thought that I'll fail' — rather than treating it as literal truth. This loosens the thought's grip without arguing with it.
source: Acceptance and commitment therapy (standard clinical technique)

title: Values-based action
content: Identify what you deeply care about and take one small step aligned with it, making room for difficult feelings rather than waiting for them to pass first.
source: Acceptance and commitment therapy (standard clinical technique)

title: Reflective listening
content: Reflect back the participant's own words and meaning to build understanding and let them hear their own reasons for change, rather than supplying reasons for them.
source: Motivational interviewing (Miller & Rollnick) — standard clinical approach

title: Evoking change talk
content: Ask open questions that draw out the person's own motivations and reasons for change, and affirm them when they appear — the person voicing change is more persuasive than the clinician arguing for it.
source: Motivational interviewing (Miller & Rollnick) — standard clinical approach

title: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding
content: Anchor attention in the present by naming 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear, 2 you can smell, and 1 you can taste. Useful when feeling panicky, dissociated, or caught in racing thoughts.
